title: Volume of a Sphere via Cylindrical Shells
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Derive the volume of a sphere of radius R by revolving the upper semicircle y = sqrt(R^2 - x^2) on [0, R] about the y-axis using the shell method and doubling the result.

steps.title: Set Up Shell for Upper Hemisphere
steps.explanation: Radius is x and height is sqrt(R^2 - x^2).

steps.title: Integrate via u-Substitution
steps.mathExpression: u = R^2 - x^2 \implies du = -2x \, dx \implies V_{\text{hemi}} = \pi \int_0^{R^2} u^{1/2} du = \pi \left[ \frac{2}{3} u^{3/2} \right]_0^{R^2} = \frac{2}{3}\pi R^3

steps.title: Double for Full Sphere
steps.explanation: Account for top and bottom hemispheres.
